import numpy as np

# Make sure by_type_year is built (same as before)
by_type_year = df.groupby(['ar', 'tegund'])['fjoldi_barna'].sum().unstack().sort_index()

# Fit a linear trend per type and project to 2030
future_years = np.arange(by_type_year.index.min(), 2031)
forecast = pd.DataFrame(index=future_years)

for school_type in by_type_year.columns:
    series = by_type_year[school_type].dropna()
    years = series.index.values
    values = series.values

    # Linear fit: values = slope * year + intercept
    slope, intercept = np.polyfit(years, values, deg=1)
    forecast[school_type] = slope * future_years + intercept

forecast

In [23]:
last_actual_year = by_type_year.index.max()

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

for school_type in by_type_year.columns:
    # Actual data — solid line
    ax.plot(by_type_year.index, by_type_year[school_type], marker='o', label=f"{school_type} (actual)")
    # Forecast — dashed line, starting from the last actual point
    forecast_segment = forecast.loc[last_actual_year:, school_type]
    ax.plot(forecast_segment.index, forecast_segment.values, linestyle='--', marker='x',
             label=f"{school_type} (forecast)")

ax.set_title("Preschool enrollment: actual and forecast to 2030")
ax.set_xlabel("Year")
ax.set_ylabel("Number of children")
ax.legend()
ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
In [24]:
growth_2030 = (
    (forecast.loc[2030] - by_type_year.loc[last_actual_year])
    / by_type_year.loc[last_actual_year] * 100
).round(1)

print(f"Projected % growth from {last_actual_year} to 2030:")
print(growth_2030)
